To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

The incidence of ciliary body and lens opacities was significantly higher in patients treated with a single-dose TBI (STBI) than in those receiving hyperfractionated TBI (HTBI), with a relative risk of 7.2.

the incidence of cataracts in patients undergoing stem cell transplantation is higher after STBI than after HTBI, and that T cell depletion, by preventing graft-versus-host-disease and reducing the need for post-transplant steroids may be the reason why we observed the lowest incidence of cataracs reported so far.

1) the use of a single dose of total body irradiation in conditioning for allogeneic stem cell transplantation increases the risk of cataract formation; 2) the incidence of cataracts is lower than that observed in other studies, probably because T cell-depleted transplants were employed; and 3) a prospective randomized trial is necessary to compare the two schemes of total body irradiaton.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the study of the relationship between cataracts and the use of total body irradiation (STBI) or hyperfractionated (HTBI) as part of the conditioning regimen for patients undergoing stem cell transplantation (SCT).
the study of cataractogenesis following total body irradiation (tbi) and stem cell transplantation in a large group of patients with hematological neoplasms.
the study of the role that the different types of conditioning regimens play in the development of ciliary body cataracts in patients undergoing stem cell transplantation.

cataract is a late complication of TBI and that the incidence and severity of this complication can be reduced by using a fractionated schedule.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the incidence of cataracts in our population was low and that the use of STBI was associated with a higher risk than HTBI.
we showed that STBI was more cataractgenic than HTBI and that T cell depletion was associated with a lower incidence of cataracts.
we found a higher incidence of cataracts in patients undergoing allografts than autografts, and in those receiving a single fraction of TBI than in those receiving hyperfractionated TBI.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the risk of cataracts is significantly reduced when the total body irradiation ( TBI) is fractionated, as compared to single dose TBI.
cataract is an important late toxicity of total body irradiation (STBI) and that hyperfractionated TBI is associated with a lower incidence of this complication.
